title: Kobalos Linux Backdoor Investigation
description: Investigate a Kobalos Linux backdoor on a high-performance computing infrastructure.
prerequisites: Familiarity with SSH and network scanning tools
outcomes: Identify suspicious services running on the target host
Detect persistence mechanisms used by the malware
Investigate data exfiltration on the target host

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Welcome to the Kobalos Linux Backdoor Investigation scenario. Your goal is to investigate a high-performance computing infrastructure compromised by the Kobalos backdoor malware. Use your knowledge of Unix/Linux and network scanning tools to identify suspicious services running on the target host, detect persistence mechanisms used by the malware, and investigate data exfiltration.

levels.title: Access the Sandbox
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the Cyber Range environment using SSH with the provided credentials for the 'cyrano' user on the target host.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox using the provided credentials for the 'cyrano' user on the target host.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Services
levels.content: Use command line tools such as 'netstat' or 'ss' to list open network connections and active services on the target host. Identify any suspicious services running.
levels.solution: Run `netstat -plnt` or `ss -tuln` to view all network connections and their associated processes. Look for unusual process names that could indicate malicious activity.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Check the list of active services for any unexpected or unfamiliar service names.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for processes that are using non-standard ports or have unusual connection patterns.

levels.title: Detect Persistence Mechanisms
levels.content: Look for long-lived processes or services that start automatically at boot time to identify persistence mechanisms used by the malware.
levels.solution: Use tools like `ps`, `pgrep`, or `top` to view running processes and their associated PIDs. Look for any persistent processes related to the identified suspicious service from Level 2.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Check the list of long-lived processes for any that are related to the suspicious service identified in Level 2.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for processes with unusual file paths or PIDs that could indicate malicious activity.

levels.title: Investigate Data Exfiltration
levels.content: Look for unusual outbound traffic, network connections to suspicious IP addresses or domains, and files being transferred between hosts to identify data exfiltration.
levels.solution: Use tools like `tcpdump`, `wireshark`, or `netstat` to monitor network traffic. Look for any outgoing connections to known malicious IP addresses or unusual file transfers.

hints.title: Hint 1
hints.content: Check the list of outbound connections for any that are suspicious or unusual.

hints.title: Hint 2
hints.content: Look for files being transferred between hosts or unusual network traffic patterns that could indicate data exfiltration.
